source: src/live.md (old Notion page, fetched 2026-09-22 snapshot, read-only fetch 2026-10-06)

claims.claim: Category: resident daemon, channels, heartbeat; NVIDIA's 'claw' framing
claims.primary_source_says: NVIDIA, 'Nemotron Labs: What OpenClaw Agents Mean for Every Organization', Justin Boitano, 30 Apr 2026

claims.claim: OpenClaw by Peter Steinberger, now an OpenClaw Foundation project
claims.primary_source_says: Steinberger joined OpenAI (post of 14 Feb 2026); Foundation, a 501(c)(3), announced 8 Jul 2026

claims.claim: OpenClaw released late January 2026 (earlier names Clawdbot, Moltbot)
claims.primary_source_says: Public as Clawdbot from late Nov 2025 (repo created 24 Nov 2025, first named Warelay); Moltbot 27 Jan, OpenClaw 30 Jan 2026

claims.claim: Past 100k stars in its first week
claims.primary_source_says: 29 Jan 2026 post: over 100,000 stars about two months in; '2 million visitors in a single week'

claims.claim: Past 250k stars by March, overtaking React
claims.primary_source_says: No dated primary source found; 391,456 stars on 6 Oct 2026

claims.claim: Project site quoted 346k+ by June
claims.primary_source_says: The figure is in an undated testimonial credited to @ycombinator, not a project statement

claims.claim: Node 20+, npm install -g openclaw, then openclaw onboard --install-daemon
claims.primary_source_says: Node 24.16+ or 26.1+ (the installer provisions Node); npm install -g openclaw@latest --allow-scripts=openclaw; onboard command verified

claims.claim: Three layers: channel adapters, gateway, agent runtime; models as provider/model
claims.primary_source_says: Architecture and agent-runtime docs

claims.claim: Workspace bootstrap files AGENTS, SOUL, IDENTITY, USER, MEMORY, BOOTSTRAP injected on the first turn
claims.primary_source_says: Plus caps 20,000 / 60,000 characters (USER.md 4,000); TOOLS.md now a section of AGENTS.md; HEARTBEAT.md retired

claims.claim: Skills precedence: workspace, .agents/skills, ~/.agents/skills, managed, bundled; ClawHub marketplace
claims.primary_source_says: Now seven tiers (workshop skills, extra dirs and plugins added)

claims.claim: Sessions in per-agent SQLite
claims.primary_source_says: JSONL transcripts are legacy imports

claims.claim: Steering while streaming: a mid-run message is injected before the next tool launch
claims.primary_source_says: Injected after the current batch settles, before the next model call; unstarted later sequential calls are skipped; running tools never interrupted

claims.claim: Four independent layers; embedded openclaw/codex/copilot, CLI backend claude-cli, ACP for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor; compatibility contract
claims.primary_source_says: Runtime id is openclaw; bundled Codex CLI backend removed in v2026.5.14

claims.claim: Hermes Agent: Nous Research, first release February 2026, MIT, Python, uv, one-line installer
claims.primary_source_says: Repo created 22 Jul 2025; first tagged release v0.2.0 on 12 Mar 2026, about two weeks after going public

claims.claim: 231k GitHub stars by mid-2026
claims.primary_source_says: Only the current count is checkable: 251,476 on 6 Oct 2026

claims.claim: hermes claw migrate imports settings, memories, skills and keys
claims.primary_source_says: Keys only with --migrate-secrets, from an allowlist; heartbeat, cron, plugins, hooks archived not imported

claims.claim: By May 2026 OpenRouter ranked Hermes ahead of OpenClaw on daily tokens (224B vs 186B)
claims.primary_source_says: No dated snapshot; on 6 Oct 2026 the single-day ranking had Hermes first (1.86T) and OpenClaw eleventh (208B)

claims.claim: One AIAgent loop (run_agent.py) serving five entry points
claims.primary_source_says: run_agent.py is now a facade over agent/conversation_loop.py

claims.claim: 70+ tools across ~28 toolsets
claims.primary_source_says: Architecture page wording; the tools reference at the same tag says ~100 tools

claims.claim: Seven terminal backends; SQLite sessions with FTS5 and lineage; pluggable memory providers and context engines
claims.primary_source_says: Architecture page at v2026.9.24

claims.claim: After roughly 5+ tool calls the agent writes a skill
claims.primary_source_says: A system-prompt instruction, plus a background review fork after 10 tool iterations (creation_nudge_interval)

claims.claim: Skills patched in use; autonomous curator; Honcho dialectic user modelling
claims.primary_source_says: Curator consolidation off by default; Honcho is an optional memory plugin

claims.claim: Skill and memory writes can be staged under ~/.hermes/pending/
claims.primary_source_says: Off by default (write_approval false)

claims.claim: Cron jobs as first-class agent tasks; ShareGPT trajectories; Atropos and Tinker integrations
claims.primary_source_says: Cron and ShareGPT verified; Atropos and Tinker shipped in March 2026 releases and are absent at v0.21.5

claims.claim: OpenClaw CVE-2026-25253 (CVSS 8.8) is an unauthenticated RCE with tens of thousands of unpatched instances exposed
claims.primary_source_says: 1-click (user interaction required) token exfiltration leading to RCE, fixed in 2026.1.29; 30,000+ and 40,000+ are counts of exposed instances, not confirmed vulnerable ones

claims.claim: ClawHub: over a thousand malicious packages, compromised publisher accounts, auto-update propagation
claims.primary_source_says: Koi: 341 of 2,857 (1 Feb), 824 of 10,700+ (16 Feb); VirusTotal 314 from one publisher; no primary source for the other three phrases

claims.claim: OpenClaw's security model treats prompt injection as out of scope; defaults assume a trusted single-user environment
claims.primary_source_says: Out of scope for vulnerability reports unless a boundary is bypassed; reinterpreted on the page

claims.claim: March 2026: China restricted OpenClaw on government and state-enterprise computers
claims.primary_source_says: Bloomberg, 11 Mar 2026, anonymous sources; some notices required prior approval only

claims.claim: An agent autonomously created a dating profile and screened matches
claims.primary_source_says: AFP, 14 Feb 2026 (MoltMatch); the user had told it to join Moltbook and other platforms

claims.claim: Hermes defaults: sandboxing on, read-only root, dropped capabilities, gateway kept from the runtime, injection scanning, MCP credential filtering, cross-session isolation, dangerous-command approval, staged writes
claims.primary_source_says: Default backend is local (no sandbox); Docker drops capabilities but has no read-only root; gateway separation unconfirmed; staging opt-in; scanning, filtering, isolation and approval verified

claims.claim: Hermes CVEs for command injection, SSRF, path traversal and prompt injection around April 2026
claims.primary_source_says: About 40 CVEs from 27 Apr to Sep 2026; April ones are auth and path traversal; command injection and scanner bypasses in May, SSRF in Aug and Sep

claims.claim: August 2026: Anthropic signed users out, cleared payment methods and refunded after infostealers harvested Claude sessions
claims.primary_source_says: No Anthropic notice found; replaced by the September 2026 threat report on stolen session tokens and keys

claims.claim: Meta Muse agent (Sep 9): web, mobile, WhatsApp; email, calendar, payments, health, shopping, smart home; isolated VM
claims.primary_source_says: Announced 8 Sep 2026; health and smart home not in the posts; Muse Secure VM with a Sentinel agent

claims.claim: Muse Spark 1.3 architecture: credential service outside the cell, OS-level approval dialogs, accessibility-tree browser without JavaScript; no classifier accuracy published
claims.primary_source_says: Muse Spark 1.3 is the model; approvals are a dialog in the client UI (not OS-level); the rest verified

claims.claim: OpenClaw ships a personal agent benchmark pack; nothing comparable to Terminal-Bench exists
claims.primary_source_says: A ten-scenario QA pack, 'not a generic model benchmark'

claims.claim: Credentials stolen are sessions, not passwords; short-lived tokens and server-side revocation
claims.primary_source_says: As a lesson, sourced to Anthropic's September 2026 report

claims.claim: Comparison table coding harness vs personal agent (11 axes)
claims.primary_source_says: Rebuilt in In one screen (8 rows) and sections 4 to 7; identity, users and measurement axes carried in sections 2, 1 and 7

claims.claim: Three lessons: compaction over months, the verifier problem, mid-run steering
claims.primary_source_says: Sections 5, 7 and 4, each with recordings

claims.claim: Layering not rivalry: OpenClaw drives Claude Code, Codex, Copilot; Hermes exposes ACP
claims.primary_source_says: Section 9
